name: Ultra-leftism
summary: Ultra-leftism is a family of revolutionary Marxist currents that stand to the left of social democracy and Leninism. They reject parliaments and elections, trade unions, national liberation struggles and the vanguard party, holding that the working class must organise itself, typically in workers' councils, to abolish wage labour and the state.
scope: Represents the council-communist and wider left-communist mainstream: the Dutch-German tradition of Pannekoek and Gorter, with notes on the Bordigist Italian strand and the later French ultra-gauche. Based on Pannekoek's 'Party and Working Class' and 'Workers Councils', Gorter's Open Letter to Comrade Lenin, and the Wikipedia articles on ultra-leftism and left communism. It does not cover the pejorative use of the term for any uncompromising sect, nor Trotskyist or Maoist groups so labelled by their rivals.

keyFigures.name: Anton Pannekoek
keyFigures.role: Dutch astronomer and theorist of council communism, author of the texts on parties and workers' councils.

keyFigures.name: Herman Gorter
keyFigures.role: Dutch poet and communist whose Open Letter answered Lenin's attack on the left.

keyFigures.name: Amadeo Bordiga
keyFigures.role: Founder of the Italian left-communist tradition named among its main strands.

sources.usedFor: Differences between currents on the Soviet Union, unions, elections, national liberation and imperialist war.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Ultra-leftists give free care as a need to be met in a communist society but refuse to look to the state to deliver it, so no clear stand is documented; inferred from their anti-statism.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Opposition to wage labour makes a campaign to improve its price a reformist goal, though workers' own wage struggles are welcomed; inferred.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Ultra-leftists seek to abolish commodity production and wage labour, so they reject the claim that markets allocate resources better.

public-ownership.rationale: Nationalised industry under a state is read as state capitalism in the left-communist tradition, not as a step to socialism.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Tax reform is a parliamentary, reformist measure that ultra-leftists decline to campaign for; inferred from their rejection of electoralism.

unions-good.rationale: Rejection of trade unionism is a defining mark of the current, and Gorter calls the old unions counter-revolutionary.

property-fundamental.rationale: The aim is to abolish private ownership of the means of production, with councils managing production.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Regulating capital is a reform that manages capitalism rather than ending it; inferred from opposition to reformism.

cut-welfare.rationale: Adherents oppose capital's attacks on working-class conditions, though they do not defend the welfare state as such; inferred.

worker-ownership.rationale: Pannekoek has workers' councils run production collectively, though the ownership is social, not firm by firm.

surveillance-ok.rationale: An anti-authoritarian current is hostile to expanded state powers over people; inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: No documented position; anti-authoritarian, libertarian-leaning leftists generally oppose state prohibition; inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Ultra-leftists distrust handing the state new powers to police speech; inferred from anti-statism.

strong-leader.rationale: Gorter insists the mass is the maker and leader of its own fight, rejecting dependence on leaders.

state-harmful.rationale: The ultra-left opposes the state and state socialism, though Pannekoek has councils exercise political functions that then wither into the management of affairs.

limit-guns.rationale: No documented position and the issue is peripheral to class struggle; adherents are not clearly split but the sources are silent.

empower-police-military.rationale: Police and army are the state's repressive arm, which councils replace; the current opposes the state.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: No position documented; inferred from anti-authoritarian opposition to state prohibition, though many see sex work as wage labour.

decide-locally.rationale: Councils build power from the workplace upward and delegates are mere messengers, which is close to but not the same as localism; inferred.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; an anti-state current favours non-punitive approaches; inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: Not discussed directly; the family is seen as an institution of the existing order; inferred.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Adherents oppose state-conferred marriage as such yet would not oppose equal access; the sources do not address it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; inferred from the left and anti-authoritarian outlook.

more-religion-public.rationale: Not discussed directly; the current is Marxist and secular; inferred.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Ultra-leftists put class above identity programmes yet oppose racism; adherents' emphasis varies and sources do not say.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; the materialist outlook inclines adherents that way; inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The current is internationalist and rejects nationalism.

gradual-change.rationale: Ultra-leftism is revolutionary and rejects gradual institutional reform; Gorter attacks compromise.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Internationalism implies hostility to border controls; inferred.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Left communists see bodies like the UN as organs of rival capitalist powers, inferred from their anti-imperialist-war stance.

free-trade.rationale: Free trade is a feature of capitalism; ultra-leftists are anti-capitalist and also reject protectionism; inferred.

nation-first.rationale: The current rejects nationalism and puts the international working class first.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Left communism arose from opposition to imperialist war, and treats state military action as serving capital.

open-borders.rationale: Internationalist logic favours free movement, though the sources do not discuss it; inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents are not clearly aligned.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed; ultra-leftists blame capitalism but distrust state-led programmes.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed; a Marxist current would say social relations, not technology, are decisive; inferred.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no documented stand.

revolution-justified.rationale: Ultra-leftism is a revolutionary current; Pannekoek and Gorter hold that only revolution by the working class can end capitalism.

experts-over-public.rationale: Gorter's liberation of the workers must be the work of the workers themselves, and Pannekoek has workers educate themselves.

central-planning.rationale: Planning is accepted but the Soviet-style centrally planned economy is read as state capitalism; council-managed planning is inferred as the alternative.

socialized-markets.rationale: Retaining markets means retaining commodity production and wage labour, which the current wants abolished.

land-value-tax.rationale: A fiscal reform of capitalism that adherents would not support; inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: A reformist redistribution measure, not a goal of a current seeking abolition of classes; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: State handouts within capitalism are a reform, not abolition of wage labour; inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: State direction of the economy is what the left-communist tradition calls state capitalism.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Spreading small private property keeps private property; the aim is common production.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Opposition to wage labour is listed among its defining positions.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Leaving money to the market keeps commodity money, which communists want abolished; inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies of employers and workers are class collaboration through the state; Gorter rejects compromise.

one-party-rule.rationale: Pannekoek condemns party dictatorship and the Russian party bureaucracy that monopolised power.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: An anti-state, revolutionary current rejects hereditary rule; inferred from its core principles.

democracy-best.rationale: Pannekoek calls parliamentary democracy a disguise for capitalist rule, favouring council democracy instead.

direct-votes.rationale: Council democracy rests on direct workers' assemblies, though referendums in the bourgeois state are not discussed.

workers-councils.rationale: Pannekoek makes workers' councils the organisation of political power in place of parliament.

right-to-secede.rationale: Opposition to national liberation suggests no endorsement of a right to secede; inferred.

natural-rulers.rationale: Gorter holds that the masses lead their own struggle and that liberation is the workers' own work.

political-violence-never.rationale: Ultra-left revolution is not pacifist, and councils are said to suppress capitalist remnants.

war-builds-character.rationale: The current originated in opposition to the First World War.

separate-church-state.rationale: Not directly discussed; a secular Marxist current would favour separation; inferred.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Clearly outside a secular, Marxist, council-based outlook; inferred from core principles.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Private security would be capitalism at its extreme; the current rejects capitalism.

military-superiority.rationale: The current opposes imperialist rivalry and the arms of rival states.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The current rejects nationalism and ethnically defined states.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Class struggle between proletariat and capital is the heart of its Marxist outlook.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Abolishing classes and wage labour implies equal provision, though the sources do not phrase it as equality of outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The current rejects national liberation but also opposes oppression; no documented stand.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Reparations between states cut across class lines, and the current rejects national liberation as a goal; inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Politically uniting nations by religion contradicts class internationalism.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Communism rests on collective production for need, and rejects market individualism.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Not addressed; the current is anti-authoritarian and distrusts duties imposed by communities and states; inferred.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents have no common stand.

limit-population.rationale: Marxists traditionally attribute poverty to social relations, not population; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The mainstream blames capitalism, not industry; a primitivist minority differs; inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; no common stand.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Councils are meant to be decided by workers, not delegated to technocratic systems; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not discussed; anti-state outlook inclines towards private communication; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: The current is revolutionary and forward-looking, not restorationist.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Gorter and Pannekoek argue from principle against tactical compromise; inferred.

direct-action.rationale: Rejection of electoralism and parliament is central, and Gorter has workers act for themselves through strikes and councils.

means-match-ends.rationale: Pannekoek argues that a party directing the workers will produce party dictatorship, so the means shape the result.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Only a marginal primitivist strand holds this; the mainstream is Marxist and productive; inferred.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Council management of production implies overcoming the split between managers and workers; the sources do not state abolition.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Abolishing money and wages implies communist distribution, though the sources do not spell out the rule.

production-for-use.rationale: Councils manage production for social needs and capitalist profit is to be abolished.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist critique of wage labour holds that profit comes from workers' unpaid labour.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Pannekoek describes the councils as the dictatorship of the proletariat that excludes other classes, but he rejects party dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Gorter expects Western peasants to side with capital, but the sources do not give an agrarian programme.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The current arose in opposition to the First World War as an imperialist war.

taxation-theft.rationale: A capitalist-libertarian claim at odds with the current's outlook; inferred.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The current stresses class collective action; inferred.

conscription.rationale: Conscription mobilises workers for their state's wars, which the current opposes.

exit-over-voice.rationale: A liberal-libertarian view alien to the current; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is not to be run as a business; the current opposes both.

positive-liberty.rationale: Inferred from the focus on material conditions of working-class emancipation.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not discussed; Marxists locate power in capital and the state, not in universities and media; inferred.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Contradicts Marxist materialism and class internationalism; inferred from core principles.

organic-representation.rationale: Council delegates represent workplaces and are recallable, unlike corporatist family and community bodies.

total-state.rationale: The current opposes the state and state socialism.

territorial-expansion.rationale: It opposes imperialist war and nationalism.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal-style oaths contradict revolutionary class politics; inferred.

bound-labor.rationale: Bound labour is incompatible with the abolition of exploitation.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not addressed; the Marxist view of ideology leans that way; inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: Not addressed; Marxists tend to treat morality as class-conditioned; inferred.

single-common-good.rationale: Class conflict is held to be real, so a single common good is not assumed; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The current rejects national liberation movements and nationalism, which includes Zionism.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Nation-based citizenship rights run against internationalism; inferred.

revive-national-language.rationale: A nationalist project the current would not back; inferred.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Councils give workers control, but retaining large firms under a vote is a reformist halfway not discussed.

school-vouchers.rationale: A market reform; inferred from anti-capitalism.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy within capitalism is not a concern of the current.

economic-freedom.rationale: Opposes capitalist economic freedom and does not tie political freedom to it; inferred.

rule-by-example.rationale: Gorter does favour small groups setting an example, but not rulers governing by example; inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: The current is marked by rejection of national liberation.

force-without-un.rationale: Opposes imperialist war whatever the legal cover.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Not directly discussed; a materialist current would lean this way; inferred.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The current is internationalist and holds that workers have no country.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Compulsion to work for benefits is hostile to those who oppose wage labour.

class-collaboration.rationale: Gorter rejects alliances with bourgeois and centrist parties and holds that class struggle governs.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not discussed; no known ultra-left call for destroying cultural institutions; inferred.

dominated-front.rationale: The current rejects national liberation movements and anti-Western fronts led by states.

workers-nation.rationale: Workers organise as an international class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not discussed; contrary to the current's egalitarian outlook; inferred.

ban-interest.rationale: Aims at abolishing money and capital altogether, not banning interest; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Contradicts class internationalism; inferred from core principles.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The state is seen as a ruling-class instrument that councils replace, in the Marxist tradition.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Nationalist assimilation is at odds with internationalism; inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy and ethnic theory that conflicts with class analysis; inferred.

proportional-representation.rationale: The current rejects parliaments altogether, so reforms to them are not sought; inferred.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; plausible for a left current but class is primary; inferred.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The ultra-left holds that leaders are permanently counterposed to the masses.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics contradicts the current's egalitarian principles; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Accountability before state courts is not a concern the sources address.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Rejects the state and defence of property.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Not discussed; equality is implied, though legal equality is treated as a bourgeois form; inferred.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Left communism is internationalist and rooted in opposition to war between states; inferred for this specific doctrine.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The current rejects national liberation yet is not documented on settler states.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from secularism and equality.

restrict-conversion.rationale: State restriction of belief contradicts anti-authoritarian outlook; inferred.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Religiously motivated state ban the current would not support; inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Pannekoek condemns the Soviet party-state and expects state functions to wither.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Parliamentary consent is dismissed as disguise for capitalist rule; inferred.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilism is a national-capitalist goal; inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Council revolution involves suppressing capitalist remnants by force.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Cooperation and class solidarity rather than competition are the current's principles.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The current rejects state repression but also parties; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Pannekoek's critique of party domination over the proletariat resembles this idea; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: Councils unite legislative and executive roles; inferred.

vanguard-party.rationale: Pannekoek calls a leading revolutionary party a contradiction and Gorter says the mass is its own leader.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Not addressed; the left outlook leans towards this; inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes are the basis from which councils emerge in Pannekoek.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The current attributes poverty to capitalist social relations.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Pannekoek's rotating, recallable delegates share some logic with sortition, but lotteries are not discussed.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: A state power the current opposes; inferred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: State price fixing is a capitalist-state management measure; inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: Pannekoek condemns party dictatorship and domination.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party rule over the armed forces is the party dictatorship Pannekoek rejects.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not stated, but council delegates are mere messengers of workers; inferred.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Pannekoek describes party discipline as rigid and suppressing dissent.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The EU is a capitalist state bloc, which the current would not endorse; inferred.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Religious hierarchy is outside the current's concerns and values; inferred.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Left communism grew from the First World War opposition and treats such wars as imperialist.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Elections of heads of state are not the current's concern.

recall-officials.rationale: Pannekoek's delegates are temporary messengers who can be recalled by the council.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; communism would remove property rather than distribute it to families; inferred.

people-in-arms.rationale: The revolution is made by armed workers organised in councils; inferred.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: A nationalist project the current rejects.

death-penalty.rationale: State execution contradicts the anti-state outlook; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The current treats national liberation as no solution and wants class transformation; inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Pannekoek and Gorter reject parliamentary bodies in favour of councils.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Pannekoek rejects party dictatorship even for building production.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Aid is between states; the current is class-based and anti-reformist; inferred.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Opposes rival state arms and imperialist war.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Presidential elections are part of the parliamentary system the current rejects; inferred.

central-bank-independence.rationale: A capitalist institution the current does not defend; inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Nationalist claims over land run against internationalism.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The current wants private property abolished, not conditioned; inferred.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The Dutch-German current rejected the October Revolution as socialist and saw state capitalism, though Bordigists use other terms.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance obligations feed imperialist war, which the current opposes.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Adherents oppose the state but also clerical power; no documented stand.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The current rejects the state and its symbolic head.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: State military force is opposed, but the current rejects national liberation too; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: Marxist materialism treats consciousness as shaped by social conditions.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Rule of the few has no place in council democracy.

leader-cult.rationale: Gorter holds the mass is its own leader.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Pannekoek's view that a new ruling party-bureaucracy arises in Russia is close to this, though the idea is Maoist; inferred.

land-redistribution.rationale: Gorter says Western peasants side with capital, and small-holding is not communism; inferred.

common-currency.rationale: Money is to be abolished, so currency design is not a concern.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Nationalist or pan-ethnic unity the current rejects.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Organising by nationality cuts across class; inferred.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Class internationalism and the rejection of nationalist state-founding point this way; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Historical materialism is the shared Marxist base of the current.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Not addressed; adherents distrust both bourgeois courts and bourgeois majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Quotas in state bodies are alien to council organisation by workplace; inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Pannekoek says councils are not formed by revolutionary groups but by fighting masses.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Hereditary privilege is incompatible with the aim of abolishing classes; inferred from core principles.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Nationalist education the current rejects; inferred.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Colonial rule conflicts with the current's anti-imperialist stance.

public-money-creation.rationale: The current wants money abolished, not a state-run version; inferred.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The current expects revolutionary crisis; the sources do not state the collapse thesis, so inferred.

delink-world-market.rationale: The current rejects national liberation strategies; inferred.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Left communists see the working class as one international class; inferred.

elective-rulers.rationale: Pannekoek holds that elected rulers in parliament escape workers' control; inferred.

minority-veto.rationale: Council decisions bind all participants; inferred.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Pannekoek says parliamentary democracy disguises capitalist rule.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Gorter holds that workers' liberation must be their own work, not the charity of privileged classes.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The current demands active class struggle though it rejects conventional politics.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, but fits the later Situationist-influenced strands; inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Pannekoek treats parliament as a disguise of capitalist rule, close to a consent argument; inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory frames the world around nations rather than classes; inferred.

party-own-road.rationale: The current rejects parties and the Third International; no documented stand on national roads.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The current is class-based and rejects national liberation; inferred.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Left communists have criticised antifascist alliances as class collaboration; inferred from Gorter's rejection of compromise.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Pannekoek condemns Russian party dictatorship, but the current rejects bourgeois anticommunism; inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Internationalism inclines against civilisational relativism about institutions; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Opposes the military as a state instrument.

paid-care-work.rationale: Wages are to be abolished, so extending them is not the aim; inferred.

office-by-exam.rationale: Pannekoek rejects rule by experts over councils; inferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Pannekoek states that council delegates are temporary messengers of the assemblies.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: A market privatisation measure at odds with anti-capitalism.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Common ownership with use-based holding is consistent with communism; inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliament is rejected as a body; inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred from the view that parliament disguises capitalist rule.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and opposition to property rights.

job-guarantee.rationale: State employment guarantees extend wage labour; inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: Left communists see democracies as fighting imperialist wars.

non-intervention.rationale: Opposes imperialist intervention but also not a sovereigntist current; no stated position.

industrial-unions.rationale: Gorter calls for industrial and workshop organisations, though not as unions in the usual sense.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from anti-state outlook.

informal-organisation.rationale: Pannekoek favours work groups and discussion circles and Gorter small groups, rather than permanent parties.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Opposes imperialism and hierarchy of states.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Councils manage the means of production, not personal belongings; inferred.

religion-illusion.rationale: The Marxist view of religion; inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The Marxist tradition regards capitalism as having created the base for communism; inferred.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not directly addressed; inferred from Marxist outlook.

socialized-care.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from communist outlook.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The current seeks society-wide council organisation, not small communities; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: Nationalist demographic policy the current rejects.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The current is communist and anti-capitalist.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Denial contradicts the left's historical outlook; inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Pannekoek condemns party dictatorship that suppresses dissent.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Religious war is outside class politics; the current also rejects national liberation.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Council democracy and Gorter's workers acting for themselves are direct participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Not addressed; class-first strands may resist this framing.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; legal recognition by the state is not the current's concern.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The current is built on class conflict and the left.

alienated-labor.rationale: Opposition to wage labour rests on the Marxist critique of alienated work.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Cultural essentialism contradicts internationalist class politics.

social-market-economy.rationale: Reforms capitalism rather than abolishing it.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Standing armies belong to the state; workers' militias are inferred as the alternative.

rich-first.rationale: Contradicts the aim of equality and abolition of classes.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Opposition to imperialist blocs; inferred, though workers' defeatism goes further.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hereditary rule contradicts the current's principles.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: A Proudhonian reform keeping markets and money; inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Not addressed; adherents distrust state-led responses.

reification.rationale: Marxist theme of commodity fetishism; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Pannekoek treats parliamentary democracy as a disguise of capitalist domination.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Council power is not bound to a liberal rule-of-law structure; inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Adherents oppose both state compulsion and religion; the sources give no stated position.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Protecting national industries from foreign firms is economic nationalism, which the internationalist current rejects.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Ultra-leftists want decisions made by recallable delegates of workers' own councils, not by a lot-drawn body convened inside the existing order; inferred from Pannekoek's council model.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The tradition is materialist and mostly silent on theology, treating religion as an illusion to be dissolved with class society rather than reformed; inferred, so no firm stand.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Ultra-leftists see capital and wage labour as the basis of class power, so concentrated wealth dominating society is inferred as a central evil.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: They oppose standing armies and imperialist war as capitalist institutions but would not campaign for reform of them; inferred, no documented stand.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: They want the state to wither and oppose state-run institutions, so a state programme of atheism is inferred as disfavoured though they are anti-religious.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: They seek to abolish the state, though councils defend the revolution by force; abolition of police and prisons is inferred from this anti-statism.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: They organise by class, reject national liberation struggles and communal blocs; guaranteed communal shares of power are inferred as rejected.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: They look to workers' self-organisation, not charity or state programmes, and see both as managing capitalist poverty; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: Pannekoek's councils use delegates who rotate and can be recalled, so limiting tenure of officials fits; inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: Council delegates are mandated and recallable at any moment, which is close to revocable delegation, but the statement's per-policy form is inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The issue was never addressed and the sources give no basis to infer a stand; left neutral.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Religious office is irrelevant to council communism, which gives no documented position; left neutral.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Their egalitarian emphasis on self-emancipation suggests equal spouses, though they rarely discussed it; inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Council communism stresses workers' self-organisation regardless of nationality and rejects national divisions; inferred, since parliamentary voting itself is rejected.

rent-control.rationale: Ultra-left currents reject reformist demands as palliatives that prop up capital and call instead for abolishing wage labour; inferred from their hostility to reforms.

abolish-ip.rationale: The abolition of commodity production and private property implies abolishing intellectual property; not addressed directly, so inferred.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Ultra-leftism rejects militarism and party or state discipline over workers and holds that the working class organises itself from below, not through drilled national youth.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Left communists reject nationalism and militarism and oppose all armies; inferred, though the sources do not discuss basing.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Left communists oppose imperialist war and military blocs; inferred from their anti-militarist internationalism.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Ultra-leftists reject national liberation and nationalist politics, but would not oppose condemning mass killing; the sources never discuss official recognition, so inferred and split.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The central aim is abolishing wage labour and the exploitation of the working class by capital owners; income would follow labour, not property.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Left communists justify revolutionary violence by the working class and class war; inferred, though not addressed as a question of personal ethics.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Ultra-leftism rejects nationalism and national liberation struggles as bourgeois, so national identity as a continuous essence is rejected.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; modern ultra-left writers (such as Endnotes) split on whether sex is socially constructed, so inferred and split.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Ultra-leftism centres class, and the sources never address feminist politics; modern left-communist thought is split, so inferred.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Ultra-leftists reject nationalism and the cult of nation, so honouring the fallen as martyrs or saints runs against their internationalism and materialism.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Council communism is a materialist doctrine and treats politics as class struggle, not a spiritual contest.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Left communism rejects the nation-state and nationalism, so a homeland as cultural centre is not their frame; inferred.

culture-before-state.rationale: They reject nationalism and nation-building altogether, and put the workers' own revolution first.

god-not-male.rationale: Materialist and atheist outlook means they do not engage with theological language; inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Materialist outlook treats religion as ideology to be superseded, so judging scripture is not their project; inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Left communism rejects nationalism and national liberation as bourgeois and holds that the working class has no country, so national-majority economic control is rejected.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Ultra-leftism rejects national self-determination and nation-building and holds that workers should unite across borders.

independent-unions.rationale: Ultra-leftists reject trade unions as bodies integrated into capitalism and favour workers' councils instead.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Pannekoek holds that socialism means the working class itself managing production and society through councils.

local-essentials-public.rationale: They want needs met communally but refuse to rely on the state; no clear stand on local public ownership is documented.

second-chamber.rationale: Council democracy has no place for a second chamber over the delegates of the workers; inferred from council theory.

municipal-property.rationale: They want means of production run by the workers' councils as a whole, not by a local community; inferred.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Council federations of revocable delegates fit the idea, though the sources do not say that decisions stay with local assemblies.

family-wage.rationale: They aim to abolish wage labour, so a wage standard is not their demand; inferred.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed; no clear stand is inferred.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed; no clear stand is inferred.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not addressed; they oppose the state but have no documented stand on money.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not addressed; anti-statism suggests sympathy but nothing is documented.

person-over-state.rationale: They seek the abolition of the state rather than saying what it should serve; no clear stand.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Not addressed; they are materialist but not doctrinally concerned with spirituality.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: They reject the state and parliament, so the question of national legislatures limiting regions is not theirs; no stand.

gm-crops.rationale: Not addressed; no clear stand is inferred.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed; no clear stand is inferred.

racial-group-interests.rationale: They reject national liberation struggles and put class above all other identities, so organising by race is rejected.

racial-pride.rationale: Class internationalism opposes racial pride; inferred from their rejection of national struggles.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: They reject national defence as serving the capitalist state, so a defence-only rule is inferred to be rejected.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Ultra-leftists treat nations as bourgeois frameworks and reject national liberation struggles, so shared language is no basis for political unity; inferred from their internationalism.

communal-electorates.rationale: They reject parliaments and elections altogether and want class-wide workers' councils, so separate religious electorates would divide the working class even further.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Their internationalism treats appeals to national defence as a bourgeois ruse to bind workers to their own ruling class; inferred from the rejection of national liberation and imperialist war.

free-public-college.rationale: Free education fits a communist society that meets needs without wages, though they would expect it from workers' own organisation rather than a reforming state; inferred.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Pricing pollution leaves commodity production and the state in place, so it is a reformist measure; inferred from their aim of abolishing wage labour and the state.

future-generations.rationale: A society run by associated producers is meant to be lasting, so a duty to the future follows, but the sources never discuss it; inferred.

women-distinct-values.rationale: They stress class over any gender or other group outlook and distrust identity-based claims on politics; inferred.

arms-reduction.rationale: They reject the framing of national safety and see state arms reduction as a pacifist illusion; the remedy for war is workers' revolution; inferred from the left-communist view of imperialist war.

open-diplomacy.rationale: They denounce imperialist war and the secret dealing of capitalist states, so open dealings are welcome, though they expect nothing from diplomacy itself; inferred.

capital-controls.rationale: Capital controls would be state economic management within capitalism, which they see as state capitalism; inferred from their anti-statism.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Pannekoek wants workers armed and organised in councils, and wants the state's monopoly of force destroyed.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Left communists opposed imperialist war and urged workers to refuse it in favour of class struggle.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Ultra-leftists reject trade unions as organs of capital, so bargaining through them is rejected.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred: state top-ups to wages are a reformist way of managing wage labour.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred: they reject state management of capitalism in general; no specific stand is documented.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Ultra-leftists reject national liberation and reformist programmes for a fairer capitalism.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Pannekoek holds that the workers must destroy the state machinery and build councils in its place.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred: Pannekoek sets out council production with a common accounting scheme rather than open experiment.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred: abolishing capital and value is the aim, so valuing nature as capital would be rejected.

sacred-nation.rationale: They reject nationalism and national liberation as bourgeois ideology.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred: a reformist demand within capitalism, though not opposed as hard as parliamentary politics.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred: they frame exploitation as class-based and reject national or regional frames.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; no documented stand.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred: Pannekoek sees workers' self-organisation as the basis of media, not state-funded broadcasters.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Left communists inherit Marxist materialism and see religion as ideology; a shared spiritual truth is inferred as rejected.

farm-price-support.rationale: Ultra-leftists reject state economic management and its support schemes; inferred from anti-statism.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: They oppose all states and imperialist war, so neither keeping nor disarming is endorsed; inferred as no clear stand.

workers-own-party.rationale: Pannekoek's later writing rejects any party as the organ of workers' rule in favour of councils, but Gorter's Open Letter defends the independent KAPD and the Bordigist strand insists on a class party, so adherents are divided.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not addressed; a ban on the practice is inferred from egalitarian principles, though they distrust state law.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Egalitarian principles imply equal rights, though property is to be abolished; inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The issue is not addressed; they reject nationalism but take no stand on language naming.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: They reject both agencies and the liberal legal order; the aim is council control of production, so private suits are not favoured; inferred.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Workers' councils are the only legitimate lawmaking body; formal roles for traditional rulers are rejected; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split between concern for human self-organisation and ecological limits.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: They oppose the state's courts and penal apparatus as class instruments; inferred.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: They reject nationalism and state compulsion of workers; inferred from internationalism.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Ultra-leftists reject trade unions as integrated into capitalism, but no stand on compulsory membership is documented; inferred from that rejection.

voter-id.rationale: They reject elections altogether, so rules for voting are not an issue they address.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Their anti-statism implies the state should privilege no church; inferred from opposition to state power.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Council communists reject parliamentary democracy as bourgeois and place power in workers' councils instead of elections.

premarital-sex.rationale: Their emphasis on abolishing bourgeois norms implies no objection; inferred, with no documented stand.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Being anti-state, they would oppose state control of communications; inferred from anti-statism.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Reformist welfare schemes that keep wage labour in place run against their aim to abolish it; inferred.

women-suffrage.rationale: Equal rights are accepted in principle though they reject voting and office in bourgeois states; inferred.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Materialist critique of religion as an ideology of the old order implies this; inferred, not stated in the sources.

race-social-construct.rationale: Marxist materialism treats race as a social product, not a biological fact; inferred.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: They distrust state bodies as instruments of capital, so dedicated agencies would be unwelcome; inferred.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Ultra-leftists aim to abolish wage labour and private ownership of production, so a right to private ownership through first claim is not theirs; inferred from that aim.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: They reject the state and its institutions as instruments of class rule, so courts of bourgeois states are not trusted; inferred, the sources never discuss tribunals.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: A materialist, anti-clerical tradition would reject literal scripture; inferred, the sources never discuss religion.

gendered-self-government.rationale: They reject national liberation struggles, so national self-government is not their project and no stand on its gender terms is documented.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Pannekoek and the council communists denounced the Soviet bureaucratic order as a new ruling class, so they would not defend it for its nationalised economy.

indirect-election.rationale: Pannekoek's council system has delegates chosen from workplace councils and subject to recall, with higher bodies built from lower ones.

national-church-status.rationale: Opposed to the state and all its privileges, they would not give a church legal rank; inferred from their anti-statism and materialism.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: They reject national liberation and nationalism, so autonomy on ethnic lines is not their solution; inferred from that rejection.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: They reject nationalism and see such votes as a way of dividing workers along national lines; inferred from their rejection of national liberation.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: They treat nations and borders as bourgeois and reject national liberation, yet do not defend inherited borders either; no stated position.

simple-living.rationale: Communism for them rests on abundance produced by associated labour, not on limiting needs; inferred, the sources do not discuss it.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: They oppose nationalism and any state restriction of movement; inferred from their anti-statism and internationalism.

equal-conscription.rationale: Ultra-leftists oppose imperialist war and militarism, and an equal draft or none fits an egalitarian stance; inferred.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Ultra-leftists reject national liberation and patriotism, so a spiritual duty to protect a national homeland is inferred as rejected.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Ultra-leftists oppose the state and its repression, so state killing without trial is inferred as rejected.

close-ties-china.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from their opposition to state capitalism, so ties with China do not appeal.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Ultra-leftists reject nationalism and national liberation struggles, so supporting national kin abroad is rejected.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Communism holds resources in common; inferred, though compensation is not framed this way.

self-ownership.rationale: Ultra-leftists stress workers' autonomy yet reject bourgeois individual rights; split and inferred.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Not addressed; ultra-leftists seek to abolish wages and money, not reform taxes.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Ultra-leftists want need-based provision after abolishing wage labour and the state, with no stand on targeting versus universality.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Ultra-leftists reject parties as intermediaries and want workers to organise themselves, but they equally reject any leader, so the statement fits only in part.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Ultra-leftists hold all capital to be exploitative, with no interest in reforming business privilege; inferred.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Ultra-leftists reject religion but denominational politics is not addressed; inferred neutral.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Ultra-leftists see technology as bound up with capitalism and want revolution, not a return to ancestral values; inferred.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Ultra-leftists oppose patriarchy as part of their anti-hierarchical stance; inferred.

national-resource-control.rationale: Ultra-leftists reject national liberation and nation-states, so national control of resources is inferred as disfavoured.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Ultra-leftists seek abolition of wage labour and exploitation, so judging distribution by origin is inferred as disfavoured.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Ultra-leftists seek abolition of finance rather than taxing it, and see reformist measures as futile; inferred.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Ultra-leftists see class as the key division and racism as secondary, but did not claim racism ended; inferred.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Ultra-leftists see law as an instrument of class rule, so the natural-law concept is inferred as rejected.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Ultra-leftists seek abolition of wage labour; automation is not discussed, so inferred at low confidence.

multipolar-world.rationale: Ultra-leftists reject national blocs and imperialism of every power; inferred, neutral.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Council communists adopt Marx's labour theory of value as the basis of their critique of exploitation.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Ultra-leftists reject patriotism and national struggles as cross-class, so love of country and workers' politics do not belong together.

material-over-identity.rationale: Ultra-leftists focus on class, but identity issues are not addressed; inferred.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Ultra-leftists reject the party vanguard and state, and they see state-led markets as state capitalism.

missingStatements.text: Workers should replace existing trade unions with factory-based organisations controlled by workers' own assemblies.
missingStatements.rationale: Gorter wants the old unions replaced by industrial and workshop organisations as the weapons of revolution.

missingStatements.text: Revolutionary movements should boycott elections and refuse to put up candidates for parliament.
missingStatements.rationale: Gorter rejects parliamentarism and urges a boycott of elections against Lenin's call to use parliament.

notes: Strands differ: Bordigists keep a disciplined party and reject the state-capitalism label for the USSR, Damenites allowed some electoral work, and the Dutch-German council communists reject parties altogether. This profile follows the council-communist mainstream. Many answers on social and cultural issues are low-confidence inferences because the tradition says little about them.
